issues.text: fitSpeaker measures once after a view is put and on each resize; it does not listen for a font that loads later. The pages load no web font (no @font-face in app/public/css; font-src 'self' unused for text), so there is no later font swap today; if a web font is added, a re-measure on document.fonts.ready is needed. Not a defect of this change and not a security matter.

At windows of about 236 px and narrower a single role word is wider than even the full-width own row, so it overflows its column (43 of 2 910 states per run); the tree before has the same overflow there. A visitor cannot put text there: the role and stage lines come from the page's own text table and the title from the repository's content. Recorded for REVIEWER, not a finding.

Not measured: the fonts of the Linux runner differ from those of this PC; the layout choice itself (which row a title takes) is the e2e test's matter on GitHub, which I did not run by the owner's rule. The security statements above do not depend on the font: the script writes only a class name.
